name: Apollo 11 (Eagle)
note: First crewed landing, 20 Jul 1969, Mare Tranquillitatis (Tranquility Base). Armstrong and Aldrin. LROC-derived position of the LM descent stage.

name: Apollo 12 (Intrepid)
note: Landed 19 Nov 1969 in Oceanus Procellarum, about 160 m from Surveyor 3. Conrad and Bean. LROC-derived position.

name: Apollo 14 (Antares)
note: Landed 5 Feb 1971 in the Fra Mauro highlands. Shepard and Mitchell. LROC-derived position.

name: Apollo 15 (Falcon)
note: Landed 30 Jul 1971 at Hadley Rille / Montes Apenninus; first Lunar Roving Vehicle. Scott and Irwin. LROC-derived position.

name: Apollo 16 (Orion)
note: Landed 21 Apr 1972 (UTC) in the Descartes highlands. Young and Duke. LROC-derived position.

name: Apollo 17 (Challenger)
note: Landed 11 Dec 1972 in the Taurus-Littrow valley; last crewed landing. Cernan and Schmitt. LROC-derived position.

name: Luna 2
note: First spacecraft to reach the Moon, impacting 13 Sep 1959 (UTC) near Autolycus/Archimedes. Approximate position (NSSDC); the impact site has not been identified in imagery.

name: Luna 9
note: First soft landing and first surface images, 3 Feb 1966, Oceanus Procellarum. Approximate position (NSSDC, 7.08 N 64.37 W); the lander has not been conclusively located in orbital imagery and may be tens of km away.

name: Luna 13
note: Soft-landed 24 Dec 1966 in Oceanus Procellarum; soil mechanics measurements. Approximate position (NSSDC); not located in orbital imagery.

name: Luna 16
note: First robotic sample return: landed 20 Sep 1970 in Mare Fecunditatis and returned 101 g. LROC-derived position.

name: Luna 17 / Lunokhod 1
note: Landed 17 Nov 1970 in Mare Imbrium and deployed Lunokhod 1, the first robotic rover on another world (about 10 km driven; parked at 38.3152 N, 35.0080 W). LROC-derived position of the lander.

name: Luna 20
note: Landed 21 Feb 1972 in the Apollonius highlands and returned about 55 g of highland soil. LROC-derived position.

name: Luna 21 / Lunokhod 2
note: Landed 15 Jan 1973 in Le Monnier crater and deployed Lunokhod 2, which drove about 39 km (parked at 25.8323 N, 30.9221 E). LROC-derived position of the lander.

name: Luna 23
note: Landed 6 Nov 1974 in Mare Crisium but tipped over, damaging the drill; no sample returned. LROC-derived position.

name: Luna 24
note: Landed 18 Aug 1976 in Mare Crisium and returned 170 g from a 2 m core; last Soviet lunar mission. LROC-derived position.

name: Ranger 7
note: First successful US lunar probe; returned 4,308 images before impacting Mare Cognitum on 31 Jul 1964. LROC-derived position of the impact crater.

name: Ranger 8
note: Imaging probe; impacted Mare Tranquillitatis on 20 Feb 1965. LROC-derived position of the impact crater.

name: Ranger 9
note: Imaging probe; impacted inside Alphonsus crater on 24 Mar 1965. LROC-derived position of the impact crater.

name: Surveyor 1
note: First US soft landing, 2 Jun 1966, Oceanus Procellarum (Flamsteed P). LROC-derived position.

name: Surveyor 3
note: Landed 20 Apr 1967 in Oceanus Procellarum; visited by the Apollo 12 crew in 1969, who returned parts to Earth. LROC-derived position.

name: Surveyor 5
note: Landed 11 Sep 1967 in Mare Tranquillitatis; first in-situ chemical analysis of lunar soil. LROC-derived position.

name: Surveyor 6
note: Landed 10 Nov 1967 in Sinus Medii; performed the first rocket 'hop' on the Moon. LROC-derived position.

name: Surveyor 7
note: Landed 10 Jan 1968 on the ejecta blanket north of Tycho; last Surveyor. LROC-derived position.

name: Chang'e 3 / Yutu
note: Landed 14 Dec 2013 in northern Mare Imbrium (IAU: Guang Han Gong) with the Yutu rover; first soft landing since 1976. LROC-derived position of the lander.

name: Chang'e 4 / Yutu-2
note: First landing on the far side, 3 Jan 2019, Von Karman crater in the South Pole-Aitken basin (IAU: Statio Tianhe), with the Yutu-2 rover. LROC-derived position of the lander.

name: Chang'e 5
note: Landed 1 Dec 2020 near Mons Ruemker in Oceanus Procellarum (IAU: Statio Tianchuan); returned 1,731 g of young mare basalt. LROC-derived position.

name: Chang'e 6
note: First far-side sample return: landed 1 Jun 2024 (UTC) in the southern Apollo basin (IAU: Statio Tianjiang) and returned 1,935 g. LROC-derived position.

name: Chandrayaan-3 (Vikram / Pragyan)
note: Landed 23 Aug 2023 near Manzinus; first landing in the lunar south polar region. Site named Shiv Shakti point (IAU: Statio Shiv Shakti). Deployed the Pragyan rover. LROC-derived position.

name: SLIM
note: Japan's first soft landing, 19 Jan 2024, near Shioli crater; pinpoint landing within about 55 m of target, coming to rest nose-down. LROC-derived position.

name: Odysseus (IM-1)
note: First commercial soft landing, 22 Feb 2024, near Malapert A; tipped onto its side at touchdown but operated for about a week. LROC-derived position.

name: Blue Ghost Mission 1
note: Landed upright 2 Mar 2025 in Mare Crisium near Mons Latreille; operated for a full lunar day (about 14 Earth days). LROC-derived position.

name: Athena (IM-2)
note: Landed 6 Mar 2025 on Mons Mouton, about 250 m from target, coming to rest on its side in a shallow crater; mission ended the next day. LROC-derived position.

name: Luna 25 impact
note: Russian lander lost during an orbit-lowering burn; crashed 19 Aug 2023 on the inner rim of Pontecoulant G. LROC-derived position of the likely ~10 m impact crater.

name: Chandrayaan-2 Vikram impact
note: Lander lost contact during final descent and crashed 6 Sep 2019 (UTC) between Manzinus C and Simpelius N. LROC-derived position of the impact site.

name: Beresheet impact
note: First privately funded lunar landing attempt; main engine failed during descent and it crashed in Mare Serenitatis on 11 Apr 2019. LROC-derived position.

name: Hakuto-R Mission 1 impact
note: Japanese commercial lander; ran out of propellant after an altitude-estimation error and crashed near Atlas crater on 25 Apr 2023. LROC-derived position of the debris.

name: Resilience (Hakuto-R Mission 2) impact
note: Second ispace lander; a laser rangefinder problem prevented sufficient braking and it crashed in Mare Frigoris on 5 Jun 2025. LROC-derived position.

name: LCROSS impact
note: Centaur upper stage deliberately crashed into permanently shadowed Cabeus crater on 9 Oct 2009; the ejecta plume revealed water ice. Position from LROC/ShadowCam.

name: SMART-1 impact
note: ESA's ion-propelled orbiter; deliberately crashed at a grazing angle in Lacus Excellentiae on 3 Sep 2006. Impact scar identified in LROC imagery in 2017.

name: GRAIL Ebb and Flow impact
note: Twin gravity-mapping orbiters deliberately crashed on 17 Dec 2012 into a massif near Goldschmidt crater (Sally K. Ride impact site). LROC-derived position of Ebb; Flow hit about 2 km away at 75.6508 N, 26.8341 W.

name: LADEE impact
note: Lunar atmosphere and dust orbiter; deliberately crashed on the far side near Sundman V crater on 18 Apr 2014 (UTC). LROC-derived position.

name: Lunar Prospector impact
note: Orbiter deliberately crashed into a permanently shadowed crater near the south pole (now Shoemaker crater) on 31 Jul 1999 in a search for water. Approximate position (NSSDC).
